tob-10468: Part I of Thomas Aquinas’s Summa Theologica takes up the grandest questions: the existence and nature of God, the creation of the world, and the making of angels and human beings. Aquinas argues each point with the cool logic of a master debater, answering objections one by one. It is the opening movement of the most ambitious work of theology ever written.
tob-4168: Ernest Renan’s Life of Jesus shocked 1863 by picturing Christ as sheer man — a Galilean dreamer whose after-fame outgrew the man. Wrought in flowing French after Renan’s eastern travels, it sold by the hundred thousand. The book marks the hour when modern doubt went public.
tob-0168: Snorri Sturluson’s Prose Edda — set down about 1220 by the Iceland chief — retells the Norse god-tales in prose, from world-shaping to Ragnarok. It is our fullest witness to the old faith. Brodeur’s Englishing is the classic version.
tob-4068: Robert Ernest Hume’s Englishing strings the thirteen chief Upanishads — the thought-crown of the Vedas, on the All-One, the Self, and freedom. His clear scholar’s hand made these hard texts open. The volume is the standard one-book Upanishads in English.
arxiv-2605-08968: Arbor polytopes are geometric shapes encoding tree-like structures, and their generating functions were conjectured to have elegant forms. Feihu Liu and Jinlong Tang prove four of those conjectures. The 2026 paper is enumerative combinatorics: turning guessed formulas into rigorous theorems.
arxiv-2605-09068: Degenerate elliptic operators — where the usual ellipticity fails — have eigenfunctions with peculiar habits. Dong-Hui Yang and Bao-Zhu Guo establish some of their key properties. The 2026 paper is hard PDE analysis in rougher-than-usual territory, where standard tools break down.
arxiv-2605-09168: Language agents act in the world, and verifying that their interventions are causal — not coincidental — is hard. Fabio Rovai proposes CIVeX, causal intervention verification for language agents. The 2026 paper is about checking that AI agents actually cause what they claim.
arxiv-2605-09268: Long conversations switch contexts — topics, tones, tasks — and models stumble at the seams. Aditya Sinha, Harald Steck, Vito Ostuni, and Matteo Rinaldi study the challenges of context switching in multi-turn dialogue. The 2026 paper is about keeping chatbots coherent when the conversation pivots.
arxiv-2605-09668: How similar are two formal languages, really? Dana Fisman and Gal Meirom tackle the question asymptotically, with Hausdorff-style metrics adapted from geometry to languages. Their framework gives the field a principled yardstick. The 2026 paper is pure automata theory on measuring language similarity.
arxiv-2605-09768: Crop diseases threaten harvests worldwide, and diagnosing them needs evaluation that is both grounded and scalable. Muhammad Arbab Arshad, Tirtho Roy, Yanben Shen, and colleagues build SAGE: scalable agentic grounded evaluation for crop disease diagnosis. The 2026 paper is agricultural AI with accountability.
arxiv-2605-09868: G-theory and the cobordism conjecture meet in the geometry of double fibrations. Cesar Damian, Oscar Loaiza-Brito, and Víctor M. López-Ramos explore that meeting point. The 2026 paper is mathematical physics where deep topology constrains real physical reality.
arxiv-2605-09968: Consolidation-expansion operator mechanics offers a unified framework for adaptive learning — consolidating knowledge, then expanding it. Debashis Guha proposes the unified framework. The 2026 paper is elegant learning theory with an operator's precision. It learns by first consolidating, then expanding outward.
arxiv-2605-10268: Agentic long-context reasoning enhanced via memory-guided rereading — MemReread knows when to look back. Baibei Ji, Xiaoyang Weng, Juntao Li, and colleagues build the system. The 2026 paper is LLM reasoning with recall. It rereads with memory as its guide.
arxiv-2605-10468: The Muon optimizer fine-tuning Adam-pretrained models — can it work, and how well? Xingyu Qu, Peigeng Huang, and Samuel Horvath investigate. The 2026 paper is optimization. It asks whether Muon can take over from Adam. Optimizers compared head to head.
arxiv-2605-10368: Forest algebras — a factorization theorem for these tree-like algebraic structures. Shaull Almagor, Michaël Cadilhac, and Asaf Shoham prove it. The 2026 paper is automata theory. It factors forest algebras into simpler pieces. The theorem holds. Forests factorize beautifully indeed.
arxiv-2605-10568: G-code generated correct-by-construction — a neuro-symbolic approach via separation logic. Yeonseok Lee develops the generator. The 2026 paper is manufacturing AI. It writes machine instructions that cannot be wrong. Correctness by construction, not testing. The machine code is proven.
pmc-13438468: A formal correction notice — amending the record on host genetic regulation of rumen 6-hydroxymelatonin and methane emissions in dairy cattle, by Zhang et al. The 2026 Europe PMC entry is a correction. It fixes the published account of melatonin and methane.
pmc-13407568: Lambs fed sugarcane silage and Tithonia diversifolia — their physiological responses, body temperature, enteric methane, and ruminal microbiota. Josiel Ferreira, Natana Mendes Marques, and colleagues run the feeding trial. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is ruminant nutrition. It tests tropical forages for cooler, cleaner lambs.
pmc-13466968: Cervical carcinoma proteomics from TCGA data — p53 shows limited prognostic value, while BAX emerges as a potential survival marker. Sebastian M. Toennießen-Klein, Dennis Rangno, and colleagues run the analysis. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is cervical cancer proteomics. It demotes p53 and promotes BAX.
pmc-13465468: Non-invasive prenatal testing for monogenic disorders — an integrated platform of single-strand DNA capture and haplotype-guided variant calling. Jie Shen, Wei Liu, Li Lu, and colleagues build the platform. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is prenatal genomics. It reads single-gene disorders from maternal blood.
pmc-13454068: Evidence-based supportive text messaging for mental health — scaling and integrating it into Canada's system, in a national policy dialogue. Belinda Agyapong, Linda Liebenberg, Ejemai Eboreime, and colleagues convene the dialogue. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is mental health policy. It texts policy into practice.
pmc-13404368: Selective oxygen reduction — through intrinsic electrocatalytic activity combined with oxygen preconcentration at non-metalated hypercrosslinked polymers. Shumaila Razzaque, Katarzyna Wielondek, Alla Dyachenko, and colleagues engineer the polymers. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is electrocatalysis. It concentrates oxygen to reduce it better.
arxiv-2606-17968: Peter Morfe and Christian Wagner study diffuse interface energies with microscopic heterogeneities, focusing on rare events. The second paper in the series tackles the unlikely fluctuations that dominate failure. Their analysis quantifies risks that averages hide. The mathematics serves materials that must not break.
arxiv-2606-18168: Dipayan Banik and colleagues find all smoke and no alarm: oracle signals in agent-authored test code. AI-written tests often assert nothing meaningful, passing vacuously. The paper detects these hollow oracles. It is quality control for the age of AI programmers.
plos-pone-0003368: Cell scientists documented a major identity switch in this 2008 cancer study. Working with normal human prostate cells, the team watched them transform from orderly epithelial cells into mobile mesenchymal cells, the same transition tied to cancer spreading. The cells swapped their adhesion modules without becoming cancerous, showing the switch itself can happen before malignancy.
plos-pone-0003468: Geneticists engineered a smarter splicing fix in this 2008 paper, aimed at spinal muscular atrophy. The SMN2 gene can partly stand in for the broken SMN1, but its RNA is mis-spliced. The team's single-vector system boosted trans-splicing of SMN2 transcripts, a step toward RNA therapies that rewrite the faulty instructions inside patients' own cells.
plos-pone-0003568: Immunologists caught two proteins parking a gene in this 2008 paper. At the pre-B cell stage, the lambda5 gene locus must be silenced and moved to the nucleus's edge, and the team showed the regulators Aiolos and OBF-1 are required for both. The choreography reveals how developing B cells lock away genes they have outgrown.
plos-pone-0003668: In 2008, Go and Konishi studied newborns with severe brain damage. Healthy babies copy an adult's mouth movements right after birth, a reflex that fades by two or three months. The team tested whether brain-damaged newborns still show this oral imitation, probing what the reflex reveals about the injured newborn brain.
plos-pone-0003768: Bartolazzi, D'Alessandria, and Parisella aimed imaging at thyroid nodules in this 2008 paper. By targeting galectin-3, a protein that helps cancer cells dodge death, they made thyroid tumors visible in living patients. The targeted scan could spare many from needless surgery on harmless nodules.
plos-pone-0003868: Mann, Sargeant, and Watson-Capps asked why some dolphins carry sponges in this 2008 paper. The tool use, rare in the wild, was studied for its costs and payoffs. The analysis weighs what sponge-carrying dolphins gain against the effort, a window into animal culture.
plos-pone-0003968: In 2008, Dansithong, Wolf, and Sarkar tested whether RNA clumps alone cause myotonic dystrophy. Cytoplasmic CUG RNA foci proved insufficient to produce key disease features in their model. The negative result shows the foci need partners to do their damage.
plos-pone-0004068: In 2008, Morino, Kondo, and Sasaki zapped mice toward better blood sugar control. Mild electrical stimulation plus heat shock eased insulin resistance in mice. The combo boosted insulin signaling through the PI3K/Akt route. The gentle current hints at a drug-free diabetes aid.
plos-pone-0004168: In 2009, Nathan Georgette built a better vaccine math tool for outbreaks. His recursive method predicted the herd immunity threshold during live outbreaks. Field survey data fed the minimum-coverage estimate directly. The handy tool tells planners how much vaccine is enough.
plos-pone-0004268: In 2009, Guzman-Ayala, Lee, and Mavrakis found cells reading faint signal strength. Faint Smad2/3 signals set low gene output; strong signals set high output. The signal dose dialed the genetic readout directly. The direct readout simplifies early embryo growth models greatly.
plos-pone-0004368: In 2009, Hammond, Loynes, and Mowbray found a late job for a fish bone gene. Bmp2b played a late role in shaping zebrafish semicircular canal ducts. The inner ear's balance tubes needed it late. The finding refines ear development maps nicely.
plos-pone-0004468: In 2009, Singh, Mohan, and Isaac found prions moonlighting in iron trade. Prion protein modulated cellular iron uptake directly. The infamous protein ran a quiet normal iron job. The finding links prions to brain iron balance. The iron function is entirely novel.
plos-pone-0004568: In 2009, Roy warned that copied genes fool family trees quite badly. Gene duplication and hidden unrecognized paralogy distorted phylogenomics. The lost gene copies misled outgroup choice quite badly. The neat paper sharpens tree building practice today. Gene duplication is common.
plos-pone-0004668: In 2009, Kijas, Townley, and Dalrymple read sheep breeds' genetic blueprints anew. A genome-wide survey of SNP variation revealed the genetic structure of sheep breeds. The domestication history emerged clearly. The work aids breeding programs. The breed structure guides genetics.
plos-pone-0004768: In 2009, a team caught monkey moms overdoing tool use for babies anew. Free-ranging macaque mothers exaggerated tool-using behavior when watched by offspring. The moms performed for the young proudly. The study maps cultural transmission patterns. The use is group-wide.
plos-pone-0357368: Couples argue, but some arguments turn ugly. This research paper looks at the harsh tactics people use during fights with a romantic partner — insults, threats, and stonewalling — and asks what role trust and loneliness play. The authors studied how feeling lonely or doubting a partner’s loyalty relates to these aggressive habits, and what the findings suggest for building healthier relationships.
plos-pone-0356768: Endometriosis causes crushing pelvic pain, and standard treatments fail many patients. This pilot study tested cannabinoid extracts — compounds from cannabis — on chronic pain and quality of life in endometriosis patients. The early results suggest where cannabis-based medicine might help, while staying honest about how much a small pilot can prove.
plos-pone-0357568: Does going online keep older people healthier? Using Chinese survey data, this paper traced indirect links from internet use to health through social participation and physical activity. The pathways suggest the web helps seniors stay healthy not through screens, but by getting them out and engaged.
plos-pone-0356468: A fish egg must pack everything the embryo needs — including the machinery to make proteins. This paper tracked how ribogenesis genes are regulated throughout egg development in the thicklip grey mullet, Chelon labrosus. The maternal contribution it mapped reveals how mothers stock the embryo’s first toolkit before fertilization even finishes its work.
plos-pone-0357668: Intussusception — when a child’s bowel telescopes into itself — is a true pediatric emergency. This study at a tertiary hospital in northwestern Ethiopia examined management outcomes and the factors driving length of hospital stay. The findings guide faster, safer care for children facing this frightening condition.
plos-pone-0356268: Infants in South Sudan too often miss their follow-up vaccines — with deadly consequences. This study tested the effectiveness of monitoring mechanisms in reducing immunization dropouts among infants in Maridi County health facilities. The mechanisms that worked offer a template for keeping babies on schedule.
plos-pone-0348968: Prescribing fresh produce to mothers — food as medicine, literally. This paper measured the impact of the Food4Moms produce prescription program on readiness for healthy eating, fruit and vegetable intake, and food security. The results test whether a produce prescription can genuinely feed families better.
plos-pone-0357268: The fat cushioning the rectum — mesorectal fat — holds hidden clues about cancer spread. This MR-based radiomics study used it to improve prediction of perirectal lymph node metastasis and extramural venous invasion in locally advanced rectal cancer. The fat-based imaging sharpens prognosis and surgical planning.
plos-pone-0354668: Predicting depression: do classic statistics or modern machine learning win? This comparative analysis pitted logistic regression against machine learning models for depression prediction and key factor identification. The bake-off reveals when fancy AI beats — or merely ties — the old workhorse.
plos-pone-0346268: Scientists’ disciplinary identities are fluid and complex — and old measures miss that. This paper validated a novel measure of scientists’ disciplinary affiliation designed to capture its complexity and plasticity. The validated tool lets science studies track how researchers actually identify across fields.
plos-pone-0354968: Field trials of wheat and cassava are noisy — but spatial statistics can clean the signal. This paper showed field trial analyses benefit from spatial correction. The corrected analyses give plant breeders truer yield estimates — accelerating the development of better varieties for farmers who need them.
plos-pone-0346668: Wastewater surveillance catches outbreaks early — but where should the samplers go? This paper used emergency department accessibility and social vulnerability to identify potential surveillance sites in North Carolina. The equity-aware siting ensures early warning systems protect the vulnerable first, not last.
plos-pone-0356068: What does quality nursing care feel like to dialysis patients in Northern Ghana? This qualitative inquiry explored their perceived quality of nursing care during haemodialysis. The patients’ voices reveal what matters during those long, repeated sessions — humanity as much as technique.
plos-pone-0353968: Filaggrin-deficient skin — the eczema-prone kind — hosts a rebellious microbiome. This paper showed the MyD88 immune adaptor restricts dysbiosis-mediated inflammation in such skin. The findings reveal a molecular peacekeeper keeping microbial chaos from becoming full-blown dermatitis.
plos-pone-0355968: Uric acid — usually a gout villain — might relate to muscle function in unexpected ways. This exploratory cross-sectional study examined its association with muscle function in underweight young women. The findings add nuance to a molecule medicine thought it understood — at least in this overlooked population.
plos-pone-0353368: Iranian English classrooms are officially monolingual — but students think in Persian. This experimental study tested translanguaging pedagogy and its effect on learner agency in monolingual Iranian EFL classrooms. The findings challenge English-only dogma — showing that welcoming the mother tongue empowers learners.
plos-pone-0352968: Fritillaria flowers and flesh flies play a visual trick — color patterns that shift with perspective. This in-depth analysis of Fritillaria flowers and Sarcophaga flies’ color-changing patterns explored how round becomes square and stripes combine. The findings reveal pollination deception as sophisticated optical engineering.
plos-pone-0355168: Glioblastoma might be attacked through its blood vessels’ telomeres — but does it work? This paper found that targeting telomeres in brain vasculature does not impede the initiation and progression of glioblastoma. The negative result is valuable: it closes a therapeutic avenue, redirecting effort toward more promising targets.
plos-pone-0355468: Termites remember trails that no longer exist — a spatial memory of vanished pheromones. This paper revisited those absent trails. The findings reveal insect memory operating at the colony level — with implications for understanding collective cognition.
plos-pone-0334868: Americans’ views on environmental regulation split along religious and economic lines — in fuzzy, overlapping clusters. This paper used fuzzy clustering to understand those religious and socioeconomic determinants of public perception. The nuanced mapping moves beyond red-versus-blue caricatures of environmental opinion.
plos-pone-0353068: Dredged sludge — a disposal headache — can become construction material with the right chemistry. This paper studied multi-source solid waste synergistic activation on strength evolution and micro-mechanisms of sludge stabilized with low-carbon curing agents. The findings turn waste into resource — literally building with dredged mud.
plos-pone-0355368: Chickenpox virus — varicella-zoster — circulates in strains worth genotyping. This Shanxi Province study analyzed circulating strains and glycoprotein E characteristics. The molecular epidemiology informs vaccine strategy against a virus that also causes shingles.
plos-pone-0353868: Parents facing fetal congenital heart defects — termination or hospice birth — make agonizing decisions. This paper captured parental perspectives on prenatal counseling and decision-making. The findings demand counseling that honors parents’ values rather than steering them — through medicine’s hardest conversations.
plos-pone-0354368: Mozambique’s HIV progress — apparently transformed — was partly a data cleaning artifact. This paper showed how antiretroviral data cleaning reshaped the country’s epidemic control narrative. The cautionary tale reminds global health that dashboards are only as honest as their data hygiene.
plos-pone-0354168: Riverside Amazonian adolescents — their menstrual dignity and experiences. This participatory study developed educational technology with them using a Paulo Freire-inspired approach. The findings center girls’ voices in menstrual health — dignity designed by those who need it.
plos-pone-0354468: Small Chinese cities — projecting their image on Douyin — navigate algorithms and culture. This paper studied their short-video communication strategies. The analysis revealed algorithmic heuristics meeting cultural resilience. The findings show how overlooked cities craft digital identities — performing for both the recommendation engine and the hometown audience.
plos-pone-0352468: Gene delivery without viruses — to liver and brain cancer cells — via engineered plasmids and nanoparticles. This paper enhanced non-viral poly(beta-amino ester) nanoparticle delivery through episomal plasmid engineering. The improved system smuggles therapeutic genes past cellular defenses. The findings advance gene therapy that avoids viruses’ risks — safer treatment for deadly cancers.
plos-pone-0352768: Ovariectomized asthmatic mice — their aortic endothelium dysfunctional. This paper characterized it. The model combined menopause simulation with allergic asthma. The findings revealed how estrogen loss and airway inflammation conspire against blood vessels — with implications for postmenopausal women with asthma.
plos-pone-0353268: Soil moisture dynamics — predicted from rainfall and soil data by LSTM neural networks. This paper built those models. The deep learning approach forecasted the hidden water beneath fields. The findings enable precision irrigation — watering crops exactly when the soil — not the calendar — demands.
plos-pone-0333868: Diatom communities — shaped by how long nutrients run out. This laboratory study showed limiting-duration effects on subsequent composition. The findings revealed ecological memory in microscopic algae. The research illuminates how resource history structures the base of aquatic food webs.
plos-pone-0353668: Colorectal cancer patients in Uganda — treatment delays and their factors at Mulago Hospital and the Uganda Cancer Institute. This paper documented prevalence and associations. The findings revealed where the cancer care pathway stalls. The research demands system fixes — because delayed treatment turns curable cancers lethal.
plos-pone-0353468: South Asian indigenous draught cattle — copy number variants characterized genome-wide with functional relevance. This paper did so. The analysis revealed the structural variation behind hardy working cattle. The findings served both conservation and breeding — the genetics of the oxen that plow the subcontinent.
plos-pone-0351768: California gray wolves — diet composition in a human-dominated landscape. This paper studied it. The findings revealed what returning wolves eat. The research informed the coexistence — the predators back, the ranchers watchful. The human-dominated landscape is the context: these wolves navigate ranchland and suburbs, and their diet shows how they manage it.
plos-pone-0353168: Critical cardiac nurses’ ECG monitoring judgment — rapid cycle deliberate practice effects, qualitatively explored. This paper did so. The findings traced noticing becoming reflection. The research improved the training — the monitor’s beep, truly seen. The rapid-cycle method is the pedagogy: nurses repeat the scenario immediately, correcting errors while the beep still echoes.
plos-pone-0351468: Stroke patients’ daily living activities at discharge — predicted by explainable machine learning with SHAP interpretability. This retrospective study built it. The model forecasts independence from admission data. Its explanations show clinicians the reasoning. The work makes the prediction trustworthy enough to act on.
plos-pone-0340568: Lassa virus nucleoprotein antibodies — an ELISA developed and qualified to detect human IgG reactive to multiple lineages. This paper built it. The assay covers the virus’s diversity. Its value is surveillance in West Africa. The work arms the labs against the hemorrhagic fever.
plos-pone-0347468: Coal under real-time temperatures — damage characteristics and constitutive modeling. This paper did so. The analysis captured heat’s role in the coal’s failure. Its mining value is deep and hot. The work models the coal that burns as it breaks.
plos-pone-0351068: Vietnamese surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis — optimized through pharmacist-led audit and feedback. This paper provided the evidence. The analysis showed the pharmacist’s eye on the antibiotics. Its stewardship value is the correction. The work lets the pharmacist police the prophylaxis. The tertiary-hospital evidence is the proof of concept: it shows audit-and-feedback working in a resource-constrained setting.
plos-pone-0352268: Bogotá’s homeless populations — AI-based disease prediction with implications for targeted interventions. This paper built it. The models forecasted illness among the unsheltered. Its equity value is the targeting. The work aims the algorithms at the invisible. The Bogotá setting is the context: Colombia’s capital concentrates homelessness where the health system barely reaches.
plos-pone-0352168: Foundation consolidation — large-deformation analysis via elliptical cylinder equivalent drainage plate theory. This paper did so. The analysis modeled the settling ground. Its geotechnical value is the prediction. The work forecasts the foundation’s long squeeze. The large-deformation framing is the realism: soft foundations settle far beyond what small-strain theory allows.
plos-pone-0345868: Older homeless adults — heart failure and coronary disease prevalence in a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol with consultation. This paper outlines it. The planned synthesis will count the cardiac burden of homelessness. The finding will guide the outreach. The protocol prepares to measure the street’s toll on the heart.
europmc-pmc2792768: When scientists map protein structures with X-ray crystallography, blurry data is a constant problem. This 2000 paper by Thomas Terwilliger presents a maximum-likelihood method for density modification, a technique that sharpens those maps. The approach improved how researchers turn raw diffraction data into clear pictures of molecules. It became a widely used tool in structural biology.
europmc-pmc2844368: Turning stalk waste to fuel stalls where juices can't touch fiber. This 2010 paper holds that poor reach curbs enzyme brews and probes fiber-loosening, the slackening of stalk weave. The authors bare the wall. Their read steers better warm-ups for fuel makers.
europmc-pmc2858668: Lung tumors look alike under the microscope but behave differently. This 2010 paper uses gene-expression profiles to sort non-small cell lung cancers and predict survival. The authors' sorting beats eyeballing. Their work moved lung cancer toward gene-based care.
europmc-pmc2872668: The immune cells in our blood carry clues about disease risk. This 2010 paper maps the transcriptome, the set of active genes, of human monocytes and links it to disease susceptibility. The authors' large survey ties gene activity patterns to illness. Their data became a resource for immune genetics.
europmc-pmc2887168: Bleeding trauma patients die fast without the right plan. This 2010 paper brings a fresh Europe-wide care plan for bleeding after major trauma. The authors' pact covers fluids, blood, and clot drugs. Their plan made life-saving care the same across the region.
europmc-pmc3000368: GC-rich DNA recruits a silencing crew in stem cells. This 2010 paper shows GC-rich DNA patches pull in the PRC2 silencer in mouse stem cells. The authors reveal the pull. Their work clarifies gene silencing control. Development genes stay quiet through this trick.
europmc-pmc3014868: Nanosilica's hazards are hard to pin down. This 2010 review finds the tiny-silica danger shifts with each product form. The authors survey the moving evidence. Their overview cautions regulators. Food, tires, and drugs all use the stuff. Each use needs its own safety check.
europmc-pmc3029168: Dengue bleeds the Americas' wallets. This 2011 paper totals the cost of dengue illness across the Americas. The authors' bill demands action. Their work justified vaccine spending. Billions vanish yearly to the mosquito. Tourism and workdays both take the hit. Vaccines now promise to stem the losses.
europmc-pmc3061868: Preemie guts overreact to germs. This 2011 paper shows an immature gut immune reply drives the runaway inflammation of necrotizing enterocolitis. The authors reveal the overreaction. Their work guides newborn care. Breast milk calms the overreaction best. Probiotics are now tested in preemies.
europmc-pmc3117868: Stem cells' energy use got mapped. This 2011 paper compares energy metabolism in pluripotent stem cells and their differentiated kin. The authors reveal the metabolic switch. Their work guides cell culture. Stem cells burn sugar; mature cells breathe. The switch marks successful reprogramming.
europmc-pmc3262968: Ovarian cancer's driver got confirmed. This 2010 paper shows TP53 mutations strike nearly every high-grade ovarian tumor. The authors reveal the ubiquity. Their work guides treatment. The finding unified the disease, they note. Therapies now target the pathway. The paper is a landmark.
europmc-pmc3269368: Cancer got an immune score. This 2012 paper proposes scoring tumors by their immune infiltrate. The authors reveal the power. Their work points to prognosis. The score beat staging, they found. Clinics now use the test. Galon's team led the work.
europmc-pmc3289668: Cancer's grip got measured. This 2012 paper shows aggressive cancer cells pull harder on surfaces. The authors reveal the grip. Their work points to prognosis. The pulling predicted spread. Kraning-Rush's team led the work. The study is widely cited. It shaped mechanobiology.
europmc-pmc3302668: RNA binding sites got PARalyzer. This 2011 paper brings PARalyzer, which maps RNA binding sites from PAR-CLIP data. The authors' tool defines the sites. Their software spread through labs. RNA labs adopted it fast. The tool is open source. Corcoran's team led the work.
europmc-pmc3302868: Cancer cells built nano-tunnels. This 2012 paper shows thin nanotubes shuttle cargo between mesothelioma cells. The authors reveal the conduits. Their work points to therapy. Blocking the tunnels slowed growth. Lou's team led the work. The paper is widely cited.
europmc-pmc3316968: An inflammation target got a heart test. This 2012 gene-based study tests IL-6 receptor blockade for heart disease. The authors reveal the benefit. Their work points to drugs. Blocking the receptor cut risk. The consortium led the work. Tocilizumab followed the logic.
europmc-pmc3326568: Immune cells predicted chemo response. This 2011 paper shows tumor-invading immune cells predict chemo success. The authors reveal the power. Their work guides cancer doctors. ER-negative tumors benefited most. West's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It shaped treatment rules.
europmc-pmc3368268: Jumping genes remodeled genomes. This 2012 paper shows jumping-gene waves reshape mammal genomes. The authors reveal the remodeling. Their work lights up evolution. CTCF binding shifted, they found. Schmidt's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It is an evolution classic.
europmc-pmc3386168: Plant ripening got a control cascade. This 2012 paper shows MPK3/6 and WRKY steer ethylene in Arabidopsis. The authors reveal the cascade. Their work guides botany. Li's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It shaped crop research. The study shaped plant breeding.
europmc-pmc3405068: A blood lipid got an obesity link. This 2012 paper shows a blood lipid drops in obesity and diabetes. The authors reveal the drop. Their work guides research. Barber's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It shaped biomarker research.
europmc-pmc6554968: Comparing invasive breast tumors with neighboring healthy tissue, researchers read the full set of active genes in each. The transcriptome sweep flagged misbehaving genes and a busy signaling lane - the ECM-receptor interaction pathway - tied to cancer's advance. The shortlist offers new suspects for diagnosis and treatment of ductal breast cancer.
europmc-pmc6600968: Growing replacement tissue needs more than cells - it needs scaffolding to grow on. This review surveys scaffold strategies for tissue engineering: the materials, architectures, and fabrication tricks behind lab-grown cartilage, bone, skin, and nerves. The right scaffold coaxes cells into forming working tissue, bringing regenerative medicine closer.
europmc-pmc6675068: The best chronic-disease care happens between appointments - when patients manage themselves. This systematic review evaluates self-management support strategies in primary care: what helps patients help themselves. The findings spotlight the active ingredients of programs that actually work.
europmc-pmc6784868: Cities were blamed for the obesity epidemic - but the data point elsewhere. This global analysis finds rising rural body-mass index, not urbanization, is the main driver of adult obesity worldwide. The surprise flips the script on where prevention should focus.
europmc-pmc6851668: Metabolic syndrome may be just the tip - body clocks run deeper. This paper proposes the 'Circadian Syndrome': disrupted rhythms as the root of metabolic ills and more. The concept reframes lifestyle disease around the clock. Fix the clock, fix the metabolism.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-168: A 2007 Government Accountability Office financial audit of the Bureau of the Public Debt's schedules of federal debt for fiscal years 2007 and 2006. The audit tested the accounting behind the national debt figures the bureau reports — the official ledger of what the United States owes. GAO's opinion affirms whether those numbers fairly represent the debt, a judgment that underpins confidence in Treasury reporting.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-68: A 2007 Government Accountability Office report pressing the Defense Department to tighten its handling of Global War on Terrorism spending. GAO argues DOD needed to encourage fiscal discipline and make better use of tools meant to improve cost reporting for the wars. The report documents how foggy accounting made it hard for Congress to know what the conflicts were really costing taxpayers.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1168: This 2007 Government Accountability Office report argues that better information and a systematic process could improve how agencies allocate fuel-reduction funds and select wildfire-prevention projects. Billions were being spent thinning forests and clearing brush, but GAO found the choices were not always guided by the best risk data. The report pushes for a more strategic fight against catastrophic wildfires.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1268: This 2007 Government Accountability Office report exposes government-wide abuse of premium-class travel: internal-control weaknesses let federal employees fly business and first class improperly at taxpayer expense. GAO documents the patterns of misuse across agencies. The findings fed public outrage over bureaucrats living large on the public dime — and pressure for the tighter rules that followed.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-868: Homeland Security's science shop filed its spending plan in 2007 — GAO's report reviews the technology directorate's budget line by line.
